title: Acabar por + infinitivo: cómo terminó un proceso

sections.content: Acabar por + infinitive (to end up doing something) traces a winding process to its eventual outcome -- perfect for a story that goes from a failed barracks attack to a shipwrecked landing to two years of guerrilla war before finally reaching Havana. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El ataque fracasó casi por completo, y Castro acabó por pasar casi dos años en prisión.
items.english: The attack failed almost completely, and Castro ended up spending nearly two years in prison.

items.spanish: Castro organizó un pequeño grupo armado que acabó por desembarcar en Cuba en diciembre de 1956.
items.english: Castro organized a small armed group that ended up landing in Cuba in December 1956.

items.spanish: Los pocos sobrevivientes acabaron por refugiarse en las montañas de la Sierra Maestra, iniciando una guerra de guerrillas prolongada.
items.english: The few survivors ended up taking refuge in the Sierra Maestra mountains, starting a prolonged guerrilla war.

items.spanish: Ante el avance imparable de las fuerzas rebeldes, Batista acabó por huir del país hacia República Dominicana.
items.english: Facing the unstoppable advance of the rebel forces, Batista ended up fleeing the country to the Dominican Republic.

sections.content: Acabar por + infinitive differs from acabar de + infinitive (which you learned earlier, meaning "to have just done something") -- por marks the eventual result of a process, while de marks something that just finished. Don't confuse the two.
